title: Close out the deletion: retro, and confirm ticfac ran it
description: Run the epic-close retro. The closeout role cannot commit its own deliverable: the executor's boundary forbids a worker writing .tick/, and the retro and learnings live there (ticfac tick 54n). Attempts 11-15 each did the analysis, could commit none of it, filed it as findings instead, and those findings then blocked this tick. Five attempts, five disjoint finding sets — disjoint rather than converging because a superseded attempt's report is lost with its worktree, so each retry started blind (ticfac tick 35h).

The deliverable itself is DONE and on this branch, written by the operator on the workers' behalf:
- The epic retro, as a note on pwp (commit 4561314e).
- The two retro learnings, in .tick/learnings.md, with a compaction pass (commit 836f2508).
- The epic record amended to stop asserting two deletions the reviewed diff deliberately did not make (commit 4561314e).
- All 21 findings from this run triaged; nothing waiting on a person.

What this tick asked for, answered: ticfac drove a real epic on herdr end to end — eight ticks, fifteen attempts, durable evidence, integrated gates, and a review that refused a diff it had concerns about. And 'extracted' is true of the code but not yet of the product: two herdr clients remain here (tlq), cloud/sandbox survived its list (g69), and ticfac has no install path at all (ticfac 2jn).

Closing this by hand is bookkeeping, not a shortcut past a gate. The gate passed; the role could not write down that it had.
